A high-throughput, low-latency reverse proxy and dense semantic vector cache for Large Language Models (LLMs).

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
As enterprise AI applications scale, direct consumption of frontier LLM APIs (OpenAI GPT-4, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude) introduces three critical failure modes:

  1. The Latency Penalty: Typical frontier LLM completions take 800 ms to 3,000+ ms per roundtrip, severely degrading interactive user experience.
  2. The Financial Bleed: Enterprise workloads exhibit significant semantic clustering—up to 40% to 70% of inbound queries are functionally identical questions rephrased by different users. Re-executing inference on every rephrase burns thousands of dollars in redundant token spend.
  3. Vendor Fragility & Outages: LLM APIs regularly encounter HTTP 429 (Rate Limit Breached), 503 (Overloaded Capacity), or regional connectivity drops, taking downstream user applications offline.

Aegis AI Gateway resolves these challenges by acting as an intelligent reverse proxy that sits between your client applications and upstream model providers. By combining dense vector embedding cosine similarity with an automated three-state circuit breaker cascade, Aegis intercepts semantically equivalent queries in sub-millisecond latency (\(<1\text{ ms}\)), slashes API token expenditures by over 70%, and guarantees zero-downtime resilience.

docs.title: The Three Core Pillars
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph P1 ["Pillar 1: Semantic Caching"]
        E["Dense Vector Embeddings"] --> C["Cosine Similarity Index"]
        C --> H["Sub-Millisecond Cache Hit (<1ms)"]
    end

    subgraph P2 ["Pillar 2: Fault Tolerance"]
        CB["Three-State Circuit Breaker"] --> F["Automated Multi-Model Cascade"]
        F --> Z["Zero-Downtime on 429 / 5xx Outages"]
    end

    subgraph P3 ["Pillar 3: Observability"]
        T["Dynamic Financial Savings Ticker"] --> W["Real-Time Control Plane (/dashboard)"]
        W --> S["Interactive Query Sandbox"]
    end
  1. Dense Semantic Vector Caching: Unlike brittle string caches (Redis, Memcached), Aegis understands intent. Queries like "How do I reset my password?" and "Forgot my account password, how to regain access?" resolve to the same normalized vector neighborhood and return instant hits.
  2. Three-State Circuit Breaker Cascade: An automated finite state machine (CLOSED \(\rightarrow\) OPEN \(\rightarrow\) HALF_OPEN) continuously monitors upstream provider health. If OpenAI trips due to rate limits or capacity constraints, traffic seamlessly fails over to Gemini or local models in under 20 ms.
  3. Live Observability & Control Plane: Aegis serves an embedded dark-mode control plane at /dashboard featuring real-time financial savings tracking, circuit breaker health indicators, and a live query activity feed.

docs.title: System Quickstart
docs.text:
# 1. Install package from PyPI
pip install aegis-ai-gateway

# 2. Launch the gateway server
aegis start --port 8000

Point any standard OpenAI SDK client to http://localhost:8000/v1:

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",
    api_key="not-needed"
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "How do I configure Docker networking?"}]
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)

Explore the documentation sections using the top navigation bar to dive deep into the architecture, mathematical formulations, deployment manifests, and benchmark methodologies.

docs.title: API Reference & Endpoints
docs.text: Aegis provides full REST endpoints compliant with the OpenAI specification, alongside custom endpoints for observability and cache management.

docs.title: 1. POST /v1/chat/completions
docs.text: Generates a model completion with semantic vector cache lookup and automated circuit breaker failover.

docs.title: Architecture & Systems Design Overview
docs.text: Aegis is architected following the Deep Module and Vertical Slice design principles popularized by John Ousterhout (A Philosophy of Software Design). Each module exposes a simple, cohesive interface while encapsulating sophisticated internal algorithms and state machines.

docs.title: High-Level Architectural Diagram
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Client["Client Application\n(OpenAI SDK, LangChain, cURL)"] 
    -->|HTTP POST /v1/chat/completions| Controller["Controller Layer\n(FastAPI Router & Observability)"]

    subgraph Aegis Core Gateway ["Aegis Gateway Engine"]
        Controller --> Engine["Gateway Orchestrator\n(aegis/brain/gateway_engine.py)"]

        Engine --> Embedder["Vector Embedder\n(Google Gemini / FastLocal)"]
        Embedder --> VectorStore[("In-Memory Vector Store\n(Cosine Similarity Index)")]

        VectorStore -- "Similarity >= Threshold\n[CACHE HIT]" --> CacheReturn["Instant Response (<1ms)\nX-Aegis-Cache: HIT\nX-Aegis-Latency-Ms: 0.18"]
        CacheReturn --> Controller

        VectorStore -- "Similarity < Threshold\n[CACHE MISS]" --> Breaker{"Circuit Breaker Manager\n(State Machine)"}

        Breaker -->|State: CLOSED| P1["Primary: Google Gemini / OpenAI"]
        Breaker -->|State: OPEN (Trip on 429)| P2["Fallback: Secondary Provider"]
        Breaker -->|All Upstreams Failed| P3["Local Mock / Offline Provider"]

        P1 --> CacheWrite["Populate Vector Cache & Telemetry Ring-Buffer"]
        P2 --> CacheWrite
        P3 --> CacheWrite
        CacheWrite --> Controller
    end

    Controller -->|Standard OpenAI Response + Tracing Headers| Client

docs.title: 1. Zero Extra External Infrastructure Required
docs.text: Many modern semantic caches force developers to deploy, configure, and maintain separate vector database clusters (Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus). Aegis includes an optimized in-memory cosine similarity engine with \(O(1)\) dot-product evaluations, enabling single-binary or single-container deployments that run with zero external database dependencies.

docs.title: 2. Strict OpenAI REST Conformance
docs.text: Aegis adheres 100% to the OpenAI Chat Completions API specification: * Request payload: {"model": "...", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]} * Response payload: ChatCompletionResponse with id, object="chat.completion", choices, and usage. * Any application or agent built with LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, CrewAI, or the OpenAI SDK integrates with Aegis by changing a single parameter: base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1".

docs.title: 3. Fail-Safe Cascading
docs.text: If upstream providers experience rate limits (HTTP 429), server errors (500/503), or network dropouts, Aegis guarantees client resilience through its multi-model circuit breaker cascade, preventing downstream application crashes.

docs.title: Request Execution Lifecycle
docs.text: This document provides a deep, step-by-step walkthrough of what happens inside Aegis when an inference request hits the /v1/chat/completions endpoint.

docs.title: Detailed Sequence Diagram
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Client as Client App (OpenAI SDK)
    participant Router as FastAPI Router (/v1/chat/completions)
    participant Engine as GatewayEngine
    participant Embed as Embedder (Gemini / FastLocal)
    participant Store as InMemoryVectorStore
    participant Breaker as CircuitBreakerManager
    participant Upstream as Upstream LLM (Gemini / OpenAI)

    Client->>Router: POST /v1/chat/completions {model, messages}
    Router->>Engine: execute(request)

    alt Semantic Cache Disabled
        Engine->>Breaker: dispatch to provider cascade
    else Semantic Cache Enabled
        Engine->>Embed: embed_text(prompt_text)
        Embed-->>Engine: 3,072d Dense Vector
        Engine->>Store: search_nearest(embedding, min_threshold)

        alt Cache HIT (Similarity >= Threshold)
            Store-->>Engine: Cached VectorEntry (similarity score)
            Engine->>Store: record_query_log(cached=True, tokens_saved)
            Engine-->>Router: ChatCompletionResponse (cached=True)
            Router-->>Client: 200 OK [X-Aegis-Cache: HIT, <1ms latency]
        else Cache MISS (Similarity < Threshold)
            Store-->>Engine: None
            loop Provider Cascade
                Engine->>Breaker: can_call(provider)
                alt Circuit CLOSED (Healthy)
                    Engine->>Upstream: generate_chat_completion(request)
                    alt Upstream Success
                        Upstream-->>Engine: Response {choices, usage}
                        Engine->>Breaker: record_success(provider)
                        Engine->>Store: insert(prompt_text, embedding, response)
                        Engine->>Store: record_query_log(cached=False)
                    else Upstream HTTP 429 / 5xx
                        Upstream-->>Engine: Error (Rate Limit / Timeout)
                        Engine->>Breaker: record_failure(provider, error)
                        Note over Breaker: Trip to OPEN if failures >= threshold
                    end
                else Circuit OPEN (Tripped)
                    Note over Engine: Skip provider immediately (0ms penalty)
                end
            end
            Engine-->>Router: ChatCompletionResponse (cached=False)
            Router-->>Client: 200 OK [X-Aegis-Cache: MISS, X-Aegis-Provider]
        end
    end

docs.title: Phase 1: Ingestion & Canonical Prompt Extraction
docs.text:
When a POST request arrives at /v1/chat/completions: 1. Schema Validation: FastAPI validates the payload against Pydantic model ChatCompletionRequest. 2. Canonical Prompt Serialization: The engine calls request.get_prompt_text(). It iterates through the message history and formats: 

user: How do I configure Docker container networking?
This canonical representation ensures consistent embedding coordinates regardless of message packaging.

docs.title: Phase 2: High-Dimensional Vectorization
docs.text:
1. Aegis invokes the configured embedder (GeminiEmbedder or FastLocalEmbedder).
  2. The prompt is converted into a floating-point vector (e.g. 3,072 dimensions via gemini-embedding-001).
  3. For Gemini embeddings, Aegis uses a resilient connection pool with a 20-second timeout.

docs.title: Phase 3: In-Memory Cosine Similarity Scan
docs.text:
1. The query vector is compared against all active entries in InMemoryVectorStore.
  2. Because all stored embeddings are normalized to unit length upon insertion (\(\|v\|=1\)), the similarity computation collapses to a fast dot product: 
    score = np.dot(query_norm, entry.embedding)
  3. Entries exceeding their Time-To-Live (ttl_seconds, default 24h) are filtered out automatically.
  4. If best_score >= min_threshold (e.g. 0.85), the request transitions to the Cache Hit Branch. Otherwise, it proceeds to the Cache Miss Branch.

docs.title: Phase 4A: Cache Hit Branch (Sub-Millisecond Return)
docs.text:
1. Response Reconstruction: The cached completion text and original token counts are packaged into a standard ChatCompletionResponse.
  2. Hit Counters Incremented: best_entry.hit_count += 1, _total_hits += 1, and _total_tokens_saved += tokens.
  3. Telemetry Logging: An entry is prepended to the rolling query feed: 
    {
    "time": "19:29:20",
    "prompt": "user: How to configure Docker container networking?",
    "cached": True,
    "provider": "aegis_semantic_cache",
    "latency_ms": 0.18,
    "tokens_saved": 22
}
  4. Header Injection: FastAPI injects tracing headers (X-Aegis-Cache: HIT, X-Aegis-Latency-Ms: 0.18).
  5. Client Return: Delivered to client in \(<1\text{ ms}\).

docs.title: Phase 4B: Cache Miss & Upstream Cascade
docs.text:
1. Circuit Breaker Check: The engine iterates through the configured provider cascade: 
    ["gemini", "openai", "mock"]
  2. Fast-Fail Bypassing: For each provider, circuit_breaker.can_call(provider) is evaluated. If a provider's circuit is OPEN (tripped), Aegis skips it instantly with 0 ms waiting time.
  3. Upstream Inference: The first available provider receives the inference request.
  4. On Success:
  5. Circuit breaker records success (record_success(provider)), resetting consecutive failure counters.
  6. Cache Population: The response is asynchronously inserted into the vector store alongside its precomputed embedding vector.
  7. Telemetry logs a cached=False entry in the rolling feed.
  8. On Upstream Failure (HTTP 429 / 5xx):
  9. Circuit breaker records failure (record_failure(provider, error)).
  10. If failure threshold is reached (e.g. 3 consecutive failures), the circuit state trips to OPEN.
  11. Aegis falls back immediately to the next provider in the chain.

docs.title: Enterprise Economic Analysis & ROI
docs.text: Deploying an intelligent semantic cache delivers immediate, compounding financial returns by eliminating redundant token consumption on frontier models (e.g. OpenAI GPT-4o, Google Gemini 1.5 Pro).

docs.title: The Cost Equation
docs.text:
Let: * \(N\) = Total monthly inbound queries * \(H\) = Semantic cache hit ratio (\(0.0 \le H \le 1.0\), typically \(0.40 - 0.70\)) * \(\bar{T}_{in}\) = Average prompt tokens per query (e.g. 500 tokens) * \(\bar{T}_{out}\) = Average completion tokens per response (e.g. 300 tokens) * \(P_{in}\) = Upstream price per 1M input tokens * \(P_{out}\) = Upstream price per 1M output tokens

The unoptimized monthly cost without Aegis is: $\(C_{\text{raw}} = N \times \left( \frac{\bar{T}_{in}}{10^6} P_{in} + \frac{\bar{T}_{out}}{10^6} P_{out} \right)\)$

With Aegis intercepting redundant queries, the net cost becomes: $\(C_{\text{aegis}} = N(1 - H) \times \left( \frac{\bar{T}_{in}}{10^6} P_{in} + \frac{\bar{T}_{out}}{10^6} P_{out} \right) + N \cdot C_{\text{embed}}\)$

Because embedding costs (\(C_{\text{embed}} \approx \$0.00002\text{ / 1k}\)) are orders of magnitude lower than generative inference, net monthly dollar savings scale directly with the cache hit ratio \(H\): $\(\text{Savings} \approx H \times C_{\text{raw}}\)$

docs.title: Latency Distribution Analysis
docs.text:
• Upstream Frontier LLM: Dominated by network transit, TLS handshakes, prompt tokenization, transformer forward passes, and autoregressive token generation. P50 latency sits at ~1,200 ms.
  • Aegis Semantic Cache Hit: Bypasses transformer execution entirely. Latency is bounded only by array dot-product operations and JSON serialization, completing in 0.15 ms to 0.74 ms (\(<1\text{ ms}\)).

docs.text:
You can reproduce these benchmarks on your local machine with the Aegis CLI:

aegis benchmark --iterations 5

docs.title: Circuit Breaker & Multi-Model Failover
docs.text:
Production AI systems frequently encounter upstream provider failures: * HTTP 429: Rate limits during unexpected traffic surges. * HTTP 503 / 504: Upstream LLM provider capacity degradation or regional outages. * Latency Spikes: Upstream inference queues causing timeouts.

Aegis implements an automated Three-State Circuit Breaker pattern per provider.

docs.title: Circuit Breaker State Machine
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> CLOSED: Normal Operation
    CLOSED --> OPEN: Failure Threshold Exceeded (e.g. 3 consecutive 429/5xx)
    OPEN --> HALF_OPEN: Cooldown Expired (e.g. 30s)
    HALF_OPEN --> CLOSED: Probe Request Succeeds
    HALF_OPEN --> OPEN: Probe Request Fails

docs.title: States:
docs.text:
• CLOSED (Healthy): Requests route normally to the provider. Consecutive failure counter is reset on every successful call.
  • OPEN (Tripped): Provider has breached failure thresholds. All requests immediately bypass this provider with 0 ms waiting time, cascading to the next provider in the fallback chain.
  • HALF_OPEN (Probing): Once the cooldown timer expires, a trial probe request is allowed through. If it succeeds, the circuit recovers to CLOSED. If it fails, the circuit re-opens for another cooldown period.

docs.title: Multi-Model Cascade
docs.text:
When a primary provider's circuit is OPEN, Aegis routes through the configured provider_cascade:

provider_cascade = ["gemini", "openai", "local_fallback"]
  1. Attempt 1: Check if gemini circuit is CLOSED. If open, skip immediately.
  2. Attempt 2: Route to openai (gpt-4o-mini).
  3. Attempt 3: Route to local_fallback if both cloud providers are unavailable.

Clients experience zero downtime and receive clean responses without being exposed to 429 rate limit errors.

docs.title: Extending Providers & Custom Adapters
docs.text: Aegis is built around an extensible adapter architecture. You can easily integrate new commercial providers (Anthropic Claude, Mistral, Cohere), open-source inference servers (Ollama, vLLM, TGI), or custom enterprise microservices.

docs.title: The BaseProvider Contract
docs.text:
All model adapters in Aegis inherit from BaseProvider located at aegis/providers/base.py:

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from aegis.core.models import ChatCompletionRequest, ChatCompletionResponse

class BaseProvider(ABC):
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Unique provider identifier (e.g. 'anthropic', 'ollama')."""
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    async def generate_chat_completion(
        self, request: ChatCompletionRequest
    ) -> ChatCompletionResponse:
        """
        Execute chat inference against the upstream provider.
        Must raise an Exception if HTTP 429, 5xx, or network failure occurs.
        """
        pass

docs.title: Example: Building an Ollama Local Model Adapter
docs.text:
Here is a complete, production-ready implementation of an adapter for a locally hosted Ollama instance:

import httpx
import uuid
import time
from aegis.providers.base import BaseProvider
from aegis.core.models import (
    ChatCompletionRequest,
    ChatCompletionResponse,
    ChatChoice,
    ChatChoiceMessage,
    UsageInfo,
)

class OllamaProvider(BaseProvider):
    def __init__(self, base_url: str = "http://localhost:11434", model: str = "llama3:8b"):
        self._base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self._model = model

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return f"ollama_{self._model}"

    async def generate_chat_completion(
        self, request: ChatCompletionRequest
    ) -> ChatCompletionResponse:
        # Format OpenAI messages to Ollama format
        ollama_messages = [
            {"role": m.role, "content": m.content}
            for m in request.messages
        ]

        payload = {
            "model": self._model,
            "messages": ollama_messages,
            "stream": False,
        }

        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0) as client:
            resp = await client.post(f"{self._base_url}/api/chat", json=payload)
            if resp.status_code != 200:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Ollama failure: {resp.status_code} - {resp.text}")

            data = resp.json()
            message_content = data["message"]["content"]
            prompt_tokens = data.get("prompt_eval_count", 0)
            completion_tokens = data.get("eval_count", 0)

            return ChatCompletionResponse(
                id=f"chatcmpl-ollama-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
                created=int(time.time()),
                model=self._model,
                provider_used=self.name,
                choices=[
                    ChatChoice(
                        index=0,
                        message=ChatChoiceMessage(role="assistant", content=message_content),
                        finish_reason="stop",
                    )
                ],
                usage=UsageInfo(
                    prompt_tokens=prompt_tokens,
                    completion_tokens=completion_tokens,
                    total_tokens=prompt_tokens + completion_tokens,
                ),
            )

docs.title: Registering Your Custom Provider
docs.text:
To register your custom adapter with the gateway engine:

from aegis.main import app
from my_adapters import OllamaProvider

# Instantiate adapter
ollama = OllamaProvider(model="llama3:8b")

# Register with Aegis Gateway engine
app.state.gateway.register_provider(ollama)

Once registered, the custom provider automatically benefits from: * Automated three-state circuit breaking * Failover cascade routing * Semantic caching of its outputs * Real-time telemetry tracking on the /dashboard

docs.title: Dense Semantic Vector Caching
docs.text:
Traditional caching systems (e.g. Redis key-value or LRU caches) match requests based on exact string equality or MD5 hash keys. In natural language interfaces, this pattern breaks down because users ask for the exact same information with different phrasing:

  • Query 1: "How do I configure bridge networking in Docker containers?"
  • Query 2: "Setting up Docker bridge network configuration guide"

To an exact-string cache, these are two separate cache misses, causing unnecessary LLM API calls and latency spikes.

docs.title: How Aegis Solves This
docs.text:
Aegis implements Dense Semantic Vector Caching:

flowchart LR
    Prompt["User Prompt"] --> Embedder["Vector Embedder"]
    Embedder --> Vec["Normalized Dense Vector"]
    Vec --> CosineSim{"Cosine Similarity\nvs Indexed Vectors"}
    CosineSim -- "Similarity >= Threshold" --> Hit["Cache HIT (<1ms)\nReturn Cached Output"]
    CosineSim -- "Similarity < Threshold" --> Miss["Cache MISS\nRoute to LLM Provider"]
  1. Vector Embedding: Incoming prompt text is converted into a high-dimensional vector.
  2. gemini: Uses Google Gemini gemini-embedding-001 (3,072 dimensions) for rich semantic understanding.
  3. fast_local: Sub-millisecond subword n-gram vectorizer for offline development and micro-benchmarks.
  4. Vector Normalization: Embeddings are normalized to unit length upon insertion: $\(\hat{v} = \frac{v}{\|v\|_2}\)$
  5. Dot-Product Cosine Similarity: In normalized vector space, cosine similarity is computed with a single dot product: $\(\text{sim}(u, v) = u \cdot v\)$
  6. Threshold Evaluation: If the highest similarity score exceeds the configured SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD (default 0.85), Aegis intercepts the request and returns the cached completion in \(<1\text{ ms}\).

docs.title: Sensitivity Tuning
docs.text:
You can adjust the similarity threshold based on your application's domain:

  • 0.88 - 0.92 (Strict): Recommended for code generation, mathematics, or factual QA where precision is paramount.
  • 0.80 - 0.85 (Balanced): Recommended for customer support chatbots, search queries, and documentation lookups.
  • < 0.80 (Aggressive): Maximum token savings; higher risk of returning loosely related completions.

docs.title: 3. Kubernetes Helm / Manifest Deployment
docs.text:
Deploy Aegis as an internal ingress proxy inside a Kubernetes cluster:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: aegis-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: aegis
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: aegis
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: techtonicshift/aegis:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8000
          env:
            - name: SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD
              value: "0.85"
            - name: GEMINI_API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: aegis-secrets
                  key: gemini-api-key
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8000
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10

docs.title: Docker Containerization
docs.text: Aegis includes an optimized Dockerfile based on python:3.11-slim for zero-dependency containerized deployments.

docs.title: 1. Building the Docker Image
docs.text: docker build -t aegis-gateway:latest .

docs.title: 2. Running the Container
docs.text:
Run the gateway exposing port 8000:

docker run -d \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -e GEMINI_API_KEY="your-gemini-api-key" \
  -e SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD="0.85" \
  --name aegis \
  aegis-gateway:latest

docs.title: 3. Docker Compose Recipe
docs.text:
For persistent multi-container workflows, create a docker-compose.yml:

version: "3.8"

services:
  aegis:
    image: aegis-gateway:latest
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      - PORT=8000
      - GEMINI_API_KEY=${GEMINI_API_KEY}
      - OPENAI_API_KEY=${OPENAI_API_KEY}
      - SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD=0.85
      - EMBEDDER_TYPE=gemini
    restart: always
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8000/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

Start the stack: 

docker-compose up -d

docs.title: Kubernetes Production Deployment
docs.text: For enterprise production deployments, Aegis can be deployed as an internal reverse proxy microservice across a Kubernetes cluster.

docs.title: 1. Complete Production Manifest (k8s-aegis.yaml)
docs.text:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: aegis-system

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: aegis-config
  namespace: aegis-system
data:
  PORT: "8000"
  SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD: "0.85"
  EMBEDDER_TYPE: "gemini"
  CACHE_ENABLED: "true"

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: aegis-secrets
  namespace: aegis-system
type: Opaque
stringData:
  GEMINI_API_KEY: "your-gemini-api-key"
  OPENAI_API_KEY: "your-openai-api-key"

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: aegis-gateway
  namespace: aegis-system
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: aegis-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: aegis-gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: aegis-gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: techtonicshift/aegis:latest
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8000
              name: http
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: aegis-config
            - secretRef:
                name: aegis-secrets
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "250m"
              memory: "512Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "1000m"
              memory: "1536Mi"
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8000
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
            timeoutSeconds: 3
            failureThreshold: 3
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8000
            initialDelaySeconds: 3
            periodSeconds: 5
            timeoutSeconds: 2

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: aegis-service
  namespace: aegis-system
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8000
      name: http
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: aegis-gateway

---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: aegis-hpa
  namespace: aegis-system
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: aegis-gateway
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 70

docs.title: 2. Deploying to the Cluster
docs.text:
Apply the configuration manifest:

kubectl apply -f k8s-aegis.yaml

Verify pod health:

kubectl get pods -n aegis-system

Internal cluster services can now route all OpenAI SDK traffic to: 

http://aegis-service.aegis-system.svc.cluster.local/v1

docs.title: CLI Toolkit Reference
docs.text: Aegis includes a dedicated command-line interface (aegis) installed automatically with the package.

docs.title: Command Overview
docs.text:
usage: aegis [-h] [-v] {start,serve,benchmark,stats,flush,clear-cache} ...

Aegis AI Gateway CLI - High-throughput reverse proxy with semantic vector caching.

positional arguments:
  {start,serve,benchmark,stats,flush,clear-cache}
    start (serve)       Launch the Aegis proxy server & dashboard
    benchmark           Run local semantic caching benchmark
    stats               Fetch live metrics from a running Aegis gateway
    flush (clear-cache) Flush the gateway's semantic cache

docs.title: 1. aegis start (or aegis serve)
docs.text:
Launches the reverse proxy and control plane dashboard.

aegis start [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options:
docs.text:
• --host TEXT: Host interface to bind (default: 0.0.0.0).
  • -p, --port INTEGER: Port to listen on (default: 8000).
  • --reload: Enable hot reloading for local development.
  • --threshold FLOAT: Set minimum cosine similarity for cache hits (e.g. 0.85).
  • --embedder [fast_local|gemini]: Select the embedding engine.

docs.title: 2. aegis benchmark
docs.text:
Executes empirical micro-benchmarks against realistic semantic prompt clusters to evaluate latency reduction and hit rates.

aegis benchmark [-n ITERATIONS]

docs.title: 3. aegis stats
docs.text:
Queries live telemetry from a running gateway instance and outputs metrics to terminal.

aegis stats [--url http://localhost:8000]

docs.title: Displays:
docs.text:
• Cached Vector Count
  • Total Queries Processed
  • Cache Hit Ratio (%)
  • Total Tokens Saved
  • Avoided API Costs ($ USD)
  • Circuit Breaker Health Statuses

docs.title: 4. aegis flush
docs.text:
Clears the in-memory vector store on a running gateway instance without restarting the process.

aegis flush [--url http://localhost:8000]

docs.title: Client SDK Integration Guide
docs.text: Because Aegis implements the standard OpenAI REST specification, migrating your applications requires zero code rewrites—simply redirect the API base URL to your Aegis instance (http://localhost:8000/v1).

docs.title: 1. Official OpenAI Python SDK
docs.text:
OpenAI v1.0+Async OpenAI Client 
import os
from openai import OpenAI

# Redirect client to Aegis Gateway
client = OpenAI(
    base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",
    api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "dummy-key-handled-by-aegis")
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful software architect."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "How do I configure Docker container networking?"}
    ]
)

print("Response:", response.choices[0].message.content)

import asyncio
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

async def main():
    client = AsyncOpenAI(
        base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",
        api_key="dummy-key"
    )
    response = await client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain B-tree database indexing."}]
    )
    print(response.choices[0].message.content)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Quickstart Guide
docs.text: This guide walks you through installing and launching Aegis AI Gateway, configuring provider credentials, and pointing your existing client applications to the proxy.

docs.title: From PyPI (Recommended)

git clone https://github.com/TechTonicShift/aegis.git
cd aegis
pip install -e .

docs.title: 2. Setting Up Environment Variables
docs.text:
Aegis supports both Google Gemini and OpenAI as upstream LLM providers. Export your API keys:

# For Google Gemini (Recommended for embeddings and completions)
export GEMINI_API_KEY="your-gemini-api-key"

# Optional: For OpenAI fallback
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-openai-api-key"

# Optional: Configure semantic cache sensitivity (default: 0.85)
export SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD="0.82"

docs.title: 3. Launching the Gateway
docs.text:
Start the proxy server using the built-in CLI:

aegis start --port 8000

Once started, the following services are active: * Proxy Chat Endpoint: http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions * Visual Control Plane: http://localhost:8000/dashboard * Interactive OpenAPI Specs: http://localhost:8000/docs * Real-Time Telemetry JSON: http://localhost:8000/metrics

docs.title: Real-Time Visual Control Plane (/dashboard)
docs.text: Aegis includes an embedded visual control plane served natively at /dashboard. It provides infrastructure operators, developers, and engineering managers with real-time visibility into cost savings, latency metrics, provider circuit breaker health, and incoming query traffic.

docs.title: 1. Baseline Dashboard State
docs.text: When the gateway launches, the dashboard displays zero-baseline metrics and healthy circuit breakers:

docs.title: Key Control Plane Components:
docs.text:
• Real-Time Financial Savings Ticker: Automatically tracks avoided LLM expenditures based on standard token pricing ($2.50 per 1M tokens).
  • Cache Hit Ratio Meter: Tracks total processed queries against semantic cache hits (\(H = \frac{\text{Hits}}{\text{Total}}\)).
  • Intercepted Tokens Counter: Accumulates total prompt and completion tokens saved from upstream billing.
  • Circuit Breaker Grid: Real-time health badges displaying state (CLOSED, OPEN, HALF_OPEN) and consecutive failure counts for Google Gemini, OpenAI, and fallback providers.
  • One-Click Cache Flush: Allows operators to flush the in-memory vector store on demand without restarting the server.

docs.title: 2. Testing the Interactive Sandbox
docs.text: The built-in sandbox allows you to test semantic caching directly from your browser.

docs.title: Test Step 1: Cold Prompt (Cache Miss)
docs.text:
1. In the Interactive Query Sandbox textarea, enter a cold prompt: 
    How do I configure Docker container networking?
  2. Click Execute Query →.
  3. Because no similar vector exists in the store, Aegis routes the query to the upstream provider:
  • Status: CACHE MISS
  • Latency: 81.39 ms (or ~1,200 ms if routed to live cloud LLM)
  • Action: Aegis populates the vector store with the 3,072d embedding and response.

docs.title: Test Step 2: Semantically Rephrased Prompt (Cache Hit)
docs.text:
1. Now rephrase the prompt with completely different wording: 
    How to configure Docker container networking?
  2. Click Execute Query →.
  3. Aegis computes the cosine similarity against the indexed vectors. With a similarity score \(> 0.85\), the upstream call is intercepted:
  • Status: CACHE HIT
  • Latency: 0.18 ms (Sub-millisecond retrieval)
  • Provider: aegis_semantic_cache
  • Telemetry Update:
  • Hit ratio instantly updates to 50.0%.
  • Avoided cost ticker increments.
  • Intercepted tokens increment by original prompt + completion token sum.
  • The Live Traffic Stream updates at the top of the feed with the CACHE HIT badge.

docs.title: Technical Polling Architecture
docs.text:
The dashboard is built with lightweight vanilla JavaScript and Tailwind CSS—requiring zero build steps and zero external frontend servers:

sequenceDiagram
    participant Browser as Browser UI (/dashboard)
    participant API as Aegis Server (/metrics)

    Note over Browser: Page Loaded
    Browser->>API: GET /metrics
    API-->>Browser: JSON {cache, circuit_breakers}
    Note over Browser: DOM updated (Stats Cards, Charts, Feed)

    loop Every 2,500 ms
        Browser->>API: GET /metrics (Background Poll)
        API-->>Browser: JSON {cache, circuit_breakers}
        Note over Browser: Live DOM updated seamlessly
    end

docs.title: Telemetry Headers & Metrics API

X-Aegis-Latency-Ms Numeric (e.g. 0.18, 81.39) Total gateway execution duration in milliseconds.
